records.source_rule: Same-rank playable cards normally resolve left to right, but a card known to be more important, such as the focus of an earlier 2 Save, is played first and must not be treated as a right-to-left Priority signal.
records.learning_objective: Apply the important-card exception to the ordinary leftmost tie-breaker.
records.critical_variable: The non-leftmost 2 was the focus of the original 2 Save and is therefore known to be the most important 2.
records.blind_answer: Bob must play the saved 2 first, then return to the normal left-to-right order.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The official important-card example explicitly overrides the ordinary leftmost order for the saved focus.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Play the leftmost 2 first; that ignores the known importance created by the earlier Save.
records.mutation: Remove the earlier Save focus and the ordinary same-rank left-to-right rule applies again.
records.noise: All three 2s being playable but color-unknown isolates importance from identity information.

records.source_rule: A known playable 5 has Priority over a known playable 4 that leads into the same player's own hand, despite the ordinary Priority table ordering.
records.learning_objective: Apply the 4's Priority Exception rather than the default own-hand ordering.
records.critical_variable: Alice is choosing specifically between a known playable 5 and a known playable 4 that leads into her own hand.
records.blind_answer: The 5 has Priority; Alice must not treat the 4 as the mandatory first play.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The official 4's Priority Exception explicitly reverses this comparison.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Play the 4 first because own-hand connections normally outrank 5s; the named exception overrides that table row.
records.mutation: Replace the 4 with a lower-rank own-hand connector outside the exception and the ordinary table comparison returns.
records.noise: No blind-play or other higher-priority exception competes with the intended 4-versus-5 comparison.

records.source_rule: When deciding whether a play leads into someone else's hand, Priority considers only the very next card, except for the explicit strategic concern of unlocking a Locked player.
records.learning_objective: Ignore longer future chains when the immediate next connector is in another hand.
records.critical_variable: Blue 3 immediately leads into Bob's blue 4 while the red line reaches Cathy's red 5 only through a missing intermediate red 4; nobody is Locked.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly says to consider only the very next card for this comparison.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Prefer red 3 because its future chain eventually reaches Cathy; longer chains are intentionally ignored here.
records.mutation: Make Cathy Locked and let the red line work toward unlocking her; the explicit Locked exception can change the strategic choice.
records.noise: Cathy's red 5 exists solely to test whether a distant future connector is incorrectly counted.

records.source_rule: A fully-known lower-Priority play can initiate a Priority Bluff; when the next player has no Prompt and sees no matching connector elsewhere, they blind-play Finesse Position and learn they were Bluffed if it is not the apparent connector.
records.learning_objective: Recognize and resolve the basic Priority Bluff line.
records.critical_variable: Bob has no clued blue 3, sees no blue 3 elsewhere, and his own hand is completely unclued after Alice's deliberate Priority deviation.
records.blind_answer: Bob should blind-play Finesse Position; if it is not blue 3, he learns that the move was a Bluff and no one has blue 3.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: With no Prompt and no visible matching connector, the official Priority Bluff example places the blind response on Bob.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Do nothing because no blue 3 is visible; that misses the Bluff interpretation created by the Priority deviation.
records.mutation: Put a visible blue 3 on another player's Finesse Position and the signal can instead identify a Priority Finesse on that player.
records.noise: The absence of clues in Bob's hand rules out a Priority Prompt before the blind response.

records.source_rule: Playing an unknown card normally triggers no Priority signal, but an unknown-card choice that would otherwise be extremely suboptimal can still trigger a Trust Finesse.
records.learning_objective: Apply the narrow Trust exception to the normal unknown-card rule.
records.critical_variable: Alice abandons the obvious globally-known red 2 into Bob's globally-known red 3 and privately knows the unknown 2 is blue 2, with blue 3 on Bob's Finesse Position.
records.blind_answer: Treat the extreme unknown-card deviation as a Trust Finesse on Bob's blue 3.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly allows a Finesse from an unknown-card play when the alternative choice would be extremely suboptimal.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Assume unknown cards can never signal Priority; Trust Finesse is the explicit narrow exception.
records.mutation: Make the unknown play only slightly worse with no obvious Tempo or connection loss and a forced Trust interpretation disappears.
records.noise: The known red connection establishes why choosing the unknown card is extremely rather than merely slightly suboptimal.

records.source_rule: The very-next-card simplification has an explicit exception when a teammate is Locked; the team should work toward unlocking that player rather than mechanically maximizing the ordinary immediate-hand Priority.
records.learning_objective: Override the immediate-connector comparison to address a Locked teammate.
records.critical_variable: The red line visibly works toward unlocking Locked Cathy while blue 3 merely gives the ordinary immediate connection into Bob's hand.
records.blind_answer: Prioritize the line that works toward unlocking Cathy rather than mechanically choosing blue 3.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source names a Locked player as the obvious exception to considering only the very next card.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Always play blue 3 because it immediately enters Bob's hand; that ignores the explicit Locked exception.
records.mutation: Make Cathy not Locked and the ordinary immediate-hand comparison again favors blue 3.
records.noise: The table can clearly see the unlocking effect, so the strategic exception is not speculative.

records.source_rule: A player unraveling a Layered Finesse may pause it to perform a Priority Finesse after an unrelated blind-play has demonstrated that the layer exists and remains unresolved.
records.learning_objective: Recognize when the Paused Priority Finesse exception is available.
records.critical_variable: Bob's first blind-play was unrelated green 1, visibly proving that the promised red layer is still inside his hand.
records.blind_answer: Bob can pause the Layered Finesse and perform the Priority Finesse.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The unrelated blind-play has already demonstrated the layer, which is the stated condition for the exception.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Force Bob to continue red 1/red 2 immediately; the Paused Priority Finesse rule explicitly permits the pause after an unrelated blind-play.
records.mutation: Make the first blind-play the actual red 1 connector and the special pause permission disappears.
records.noise: Bob's other fully-known playable card exists only to provide a valid Priority Finesse opportunity once the pause is licensed.

records.source_rule: A Paused Priority Finesse is not allowed when the prior blind-play was the actual connector of the original Layered Finesse, because the team has not learned that another promised layer remains.
records.learning_objective: Reject the Paused Priority Finesse when the layer has not been demonstrated by an unrelated card.
records.critical_variable: Bob's first blind-play is the actual red 1 connector rather than an unrelated card from a layer.
records.blind_answer: Bob must continue resolving the original Finesse rather than pause for a new Priority Finesse.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly says the pause cannot occur after the real red 1 because red 2 has not been demonstrated to the team.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Play the unrelated fully-known card to send a new Priority signal; this would interrupt an undemonstrated remaining Finesse.
records.mutation: Replace the red 1 blind-play with an unrelated green 1 from the layer and the Paused Priority Finesse can become available.
records.noise: The available Priority play is intentionally valid in isolation so the deciding variable is solely whether the layer was demonstrated.

records.source_rule: Unknown-card plays normally trigger no Priority signal; the Trust exception requires the choice to be extremely suboptimal without the hidden message, not merely a small Priority preference.
records.learning_objective: Keep the Trust threshold narrow and reject a forced signal for a merely slightly worse unknown play.
records.critical_variable: The unknown play loses no clear Tempo or obvious connection and is only slightly worse than the known option.
records.blind_answer: The team must not force a Trust Finesse interpretation from this slight preference alone.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The official Trust rule uses an extreme-suboptimality threshold.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat any unknown-card Priority deviation as Trust; that would contradict the normal rule that unknown-card plays trigger nothing special.
records.mutation: Make the unknown choice abandon obvious high-value teamwork and become extremely suboptimal; a Trust Finesse can then be signaled.
records.noise: The absence of Tempo loss and obvious connections is necessary to establish that the difference is only slight.

records.source_rule: Among fully-known playable cards, a card that leads into a clued or known card in someone else's hand has higher Priority than a card that leads into the player's own hand.
records.learning_objective: Apply the basic ordering between someone-else's-hand and own-hand connections.
records.critical_variable: Blue 2 immediately leads into Bob's known blue 3 while red 2 leads only into Alice's own known red 3, with no higher exception active.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The Priority table places cards leading into someone else's hand above cards leading into the player's own hand.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Play red 2 first; absent an exception, that is a meaningful Priority deviation.
records.mutation: Make the red card a blind-play and the highest Priority category would override this comparison.
records.noise: The prompt explicitly removes blind-play and special-exception cases so only the table ordering remains.

records.source_rule: A visible next connector in someone else's non-Finesse Position turns off Priority Finesses and commits the team to a direct Load Clue; it remains a Load Clue even if it would otherwise look like a Save Clue, and the receiver reinterprets it as a normal Play Clue.
records.learning_objective: Apply Load Clue despite a Save-looking clue shape and rewind Priority-related notes.
records.critical_variable: The actual next connector is visible in Cathy's hand but is not on her Finesse Position, and the required direct clue superficially resembles a Save Clue.
records.blind_answer: Bob must give the Load Clue; Cathy must abandon the false Priority Finesse notes and interpret it as a normal Play Clue.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly says Priority Finesses turn off for visible non-Finesse-position connectors and that Save-looking clues are still Load Clues.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Let Cathy blind-play because the direct clue looks like a Save; that permits the exact impending misplay Load Clue exists to prevent.
records.mutation: Move the connector onto Cathy's Finesse Position and a normal Priority Finesse can become available instead of a Load Clue.
records.noise: The Save-looking shape is intentional because the rule explicitly states that this appearance does not cancel Load Clue status.

records.source_rule: A fully-known card played over an unknown playable card can trigger Priority only if the known card has lower Priority than every possible identity of the unknown card.
records.learning_objective: Reject a forced Priority signal when an unknown card's possible identities straddle the known card in Priority.
records.critical_variable: Red 3 has lower Priority than one possible identity of the unknown card but higher Priority than another.
records.blind_answer: A Priority signal is forced only if the known play is lower Priority than every unknown possibility; this mixed superposition does not qualify.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly requires the played known card to be lower Priority than every possible identity of the unknown card.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Infer Priority from one higher-priority possibility while ignoring the lower-priority possibility; that violates the every-possibility test.
records.mutation: Raise the Priority of every remaining unknown identity above red 3 and the known-card play can then trigger Priority.
records.noise: The two remaining identities are deliberately placed on opposite sides of red 3 to isolate the superposition rule.

records.source_rule: A Priority Finesse follows the visible matching connector rather than automatically targeting the very next player; if Bob sees the connector on Cathy's Finesse Position, Bob waits and Cathy blind-plays on her turn.
records.learning_objective: Identify the actual Priority Finesse target from the visible connector position.
records.critical_variable: Bob has no clued blue 3 but sees a playable blue 3 on Cathy's Finesse Position after Alice's Priority deviation.
records.blind_answer: Bob must not blind-play his own Finesse Position; Cathy is the Priority Finesse target.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The official Priority Finesse example has Bob do something unrelated when he sees the matching connector on Cathy's Finesse Position.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Blind-play Bob's Finesse Position solely because he is next; the visible connector identifies Cathy instead.
records.mutation: Remove the visible connector from Cathy and leave no Prompt or visible match; the Priority signal can move to Bob's own blind response or Bluff logic.
records.noise: Bob being next is included specifically to test that turn order does not override the visible connector target.
